entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Full six-person parler, finir and attendre paradigms; stem extraction, on agreement and -ii-/soft-consonant spelling are taught and constructed in new contexts.

entries.source_title: Special cases when the past participle agrees (in number & gender) when used with 'avoir' in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Preceding le/la/les and relative que trigger agreement with their direct-object referent; indirect objects do not. Additional contrasts treat infinitive agency, causative fait, en and measures.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: All six être subjunctives are displayed, including soyons/soyez and distinct singular/plural spellings; prompts require sois, soient and soyons.

entries.source_title: Entrer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Contrasts entering a destination with entering data, gives the être paradigm and avoir forms, and requires est entrée versus avons entré according to direct-object structure.

entries.source_title: Sortir can be used with avoir or être in Le Passé Composé depending on its meaning in French
entries.evidence: Going out and taking objects out receive separate original examples and auxiliary/agreement exercises: a sorti les poubelles versus sont sorties du bâtiment.

entries.source_title: Conjugate aller in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Aller has a full aill-/all- paradigm with natural singular and nous examples; constructed answers sample both stems.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Full fass- paradigm is distinguished from indicative fais- and future fer-; nous, on and vous forms are independently produced.

entries.source_title: Descendre can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Teaches three constructions: own downward movement, moving cargo down, and traversing a directly named staircase. Items test être agreement and both avoir readings.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Aie/aies/ait/ayons/ayez/aient are all taught, with orthographic contrasts and production of first, second and third-person forms.

entries.source_title: Monter can be used with avoir or être in Le Passé Composé depending on its meaning in French
entries.evidence: Contrasts own upward movement, carrying something up and traversing stairs/floors as direct objects. Each construction is taught and exercised.

entries.source_title: Conjugate prendre and derivatives in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Full prendre, comprendre and apprendre person series distinguish prenn- from pren-. Derivative transfer is assessed with comprendre, apprendre, reprendre and surprendre.

entries.source_title: Conjugate cueillir and derivatives in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Complete cueillir, accueillir and recueillir futures and distinct meanings are taught; all three verbs receive constructed-response evidence with the cueiller- stem.

entries.source_title: Il faut que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) in French
entries.evidence: Explains impersonal necessity, contrasts il faut + infinitive with a separately subjected que-clause, and requires venir/pouvoir subjunctives.

entries.source_title: Retourner can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Returning to a place, turning an object over and returning a parcel are explicitly differentiated, with exercises for all three readings.

entries.source_title: Vouloir que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = To want someone to do something in French
entries.evidence: Contrasts same-subject vouloir + infinitive with vouloir/voudrais que + another subject and subjunctive; exercises distinguish both structures and courtesy.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: All six puiss- forms are displayed; the ability/permission meaning and nous/vous/ils endings are taught and produced.

entries.source_title: Rentrer can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Contrasts returning home with bringing plants/bicycles inside; exercises require the auxiliary and agreement appropriate to each construction.

entries.source_title: Conjugate venir/tenir and derivatives in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Complete venir/tenir and revenir/obtenir series explain vienn-/ven- and tienn-/ten-. Construction exercises also transfer the rules to maintenir, devenir and retenir.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Full sach- paradigm and savoir + infinitive meaning are given; singular and plural answers are constructed rather than only recognized.

entries.source_title: Aimer que/détester que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = to like/hate that in French
entries.evidence: Both positive and negative emotional attitudes have examples and distinct exercises; explicit discussion prevents the false inference that subjunctive makes a real habit uncertain.

entries.source_title: Conjugate irregular être/avoir/savoir in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.evidence: Tu/nous/vous paradigms for être, avoir and savoir include meanings, no-subject syntax and register constraints; each named verb is independently exercised.

entries.source_title: Repasser can be used with avoir or être in compound tenses depending on its meaning in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.evidence: Calling by again usually takes être, but intransitive avoir is also taught and accepted in the return-visit item. Ironing a direct object takes avoir. Examples and independent items distinguish the meanings without banning a valid auxiliary variant.

entries.source_title: J'allais + [infinitive] to express the near future in the past in French
entries.evidence: All six imperfect aller + infinitive forms are explained as past projection, with both interrupted and fulfilled plans; exercises form the construction and reject an automatic non-fulfilment inference.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: Six-person imperfect avoir series combines with -é, -i and -u participles; earlier-past examples and items include finir, attendre and envoyer with preceding-object agreement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être/avoir/faire/prendre/vouloir (+ avoir) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: Lists and exemplifies été, eu, fait, pris and voulu with the complete auxiliary series; each of the five named verbs has a separate constructed item.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: Complete être pluperfect paradigm, subject agreement and transitive movement exceptions are taught; partir/rentrer contrast with transitive sortir in the exercises.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: The full reflexive se lever person series, negative order and direct/indirect agreement contrast are taught; items contrast s'était levée with s'étaient parlé.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the subjunctive present in French (Le Subjonctif Présent)
entries.evidence: Six-person veuill-/voul- paradigm and natural concessive uses distinguish subjunctive vouloir from a main-clause vouloir that selects another verb's subjunctive.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: All persons of avais...avaient dû are taught with infinitive complements, circumflex and earlier-necessity meaning; production distinguishes this from retrospective conditional advice.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the pluperfect tense in French (Le Plus-que-Parfait)
entries.evidence: Full avoir-imperfect + pu series is tied to earlier ability and realized opportunity, not automatically an unrealized could-have reading.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.evidence: Full conditional avoir series with regular -é/-i/-u participles and unreal-past use; separate items require regular finir, attendre and terminer.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs with irregular past participles in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.evidence: Irregular participles eu, été, fait, pris, compris, vu, reçu and voulu are supplied with the complete auxiliary pattern; exercises construct avoir, être, vouloir and prendre forms.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the conditional past in French (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.evidence: Complete serais...seraient paradigm, reflexive placement and gender/number agreement are illustrated and exercised with partir, venir and se préparer.

entries.source_title: Conjugate devoir in the conditional past in French = should have (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.evidence: Six-person aurais...auraient dû series expresses retrospective advice; negative should-not-have order and accent preservation receive independent items.

entries.source_title: Il est [adjectif] que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = It is [adjective] for [someone] to ... in French
entries.evidence: Evaluative important/nécessaire/regrettable select subjunctive; general actions use de + infinitive. Contrasts certain/évident/vrai + indicative avoid an overbroad all-adjectives rule.

entries.source_title: Conjugate pouvoir in the conditional past in French = could have (Le Conditionnel Passé)
entries.evidence: Complete aurais...auraient pu series and contrasts between missed opportunity, possible past explanation and actual past ability; contextual production items make the intended reading clear.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er, -ir, -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.evidence: Full future avoir paradigm combines with -é/-i/-u participles; choisir, vendre and terminer are independently formed for completion before future points.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir/être/faire and other irregular verbs in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.evidence: Irregular eu, été, fait, pris, compris, vu, lu and reçu are taught with complete future auxiliaries; named avoir/être/faire plus prendre/lire receive constructed evidence.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs (+ être) in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.evidence: All future être persons, subject agreement, reflexive forms and movement-object exceptions are explained; revenir, partir, se préparer and arriver are exercised.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir/pouvoir/devoir in the future perfect in French (Le Futur Antérieur)
entries.evidence: All persons of future avoir with voulu/pu/dû; examples distinguish future-completed opportunity/necessity from inferred past intention. Each modal is constructed and the conjectural reading is checked.

entries.source_title: Recognising être in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Complete fus...furent paradigm and fut/fût distinction support reading. Items identify the infinitive and retell fut using everyday a été; routine literary production is not required.

entries.source_title: Recognising faire in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Full fis...firent series and original narrative uses are decoded into the infinitive and conversational avons fait.

entries.source_title: Recognising all -er verbs - including aller - in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: All -er endings, full aller series and manger/commencer spelling adjustments are taught; learners identify and retell literary forms rather than manufacture routine spoken passé simple.

entries.source_title: Recognising -ir verbs in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Full finir and partir i-family patterns, choisir/dormir uses and the venir exception; exercises decode forms and transfer them to ordinary narration.

entries.source_title: Conjugate s'asseoir in the future tense in French (Le Futur Simple)
entries.evidence: Both complete assiér- and assoir- futures are taught with reflexive pronouns, negation and action/state contrast; answer keys accept both standard series.

entries.source_title: Recognising avoir in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Full eus...eurent series and eut/eût distinction are displayed; learners identify avoir and retell eurent with ont eu.

entries.source_title: Recognising regular -dre verbs in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Complete vendre i-family series extends to attendre/répondre, while prendre is explicitly excluded from the regular rule. Items decode all three regular families in context.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs in the subjunctive past in French (Le Subjonctif Passé)
entries.evidence: Complete subjunctive avoir/être and reflexive person series combine with regular/irregular participles, agreement and negation; contrasts prior completion, future deadlines and present/later events.

entries.source_title: Recognising voir/vivre in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: Complete vis...virent and vécus...vécurent paradigms, contextual ambiguity of vis, and long-but-bounded narrative events. Both verbs receive recognition and everyday retelling tasks.

entries.source_title: Recognising venir/tenir and derivatives in the historic past in French (Le Passé Simple)
entries.evidence: All venir/tenir persons and full revenir/obtenir derivative series show the -in- family; recognition/retelling extends to maintenir and devenir without requiring literary production.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.evidence: Both veuille/veuillons/veuillez and veux/voulons/voulez series appear with usage limits. Formal veuillez and valid conversational ne m'en veux/veuille pas are exercised, while rare elevated veuillons remains recognition-focused.

entries.source_title: Plus de ... que/Moins de ... que/Autant de ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As much/many ... as (Comparisons with Nouns in French)
entries.evidence: Plus/moins/autant de with countable and uncountable nouns, elision and que comparison are contrasted with aussi and post-noun de plus; each quantity operator is constructed.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Direct Object Pronoun + Indirect Object Pronoun
entries.evidence: Explains the full ordering slots, first/second-person versus lui/leur order, auxiliary/infinitive placement and agreement; items require both groups, not a single memorized le lui.

entries.source_title: Dans lequel/laquelle : alternative to où with places (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Spatial où/dans lequel alternatives, all gender/number forms and the time-relative limitation are explicitly contrasted and tested.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Reflexive Pronoun + Direct Object Pronoun
entries.evidence: Reflexive pronouns occupy the first slot before direct le/la/les; se laver les mains versus se les laver also teaches the resulting preceding-object agreement.

entries.source_title: Tout ce qui/Tout ce que = All/everything that (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Neutral everything-that constructions are chosen from subject/object function, including an intervening object pronoun and qu' elision, rather than the next-word shortcut.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Indirect Object Pronoun + "en"
entries.evidence: Me/te/lui/nous/vous/leur before en, de-complement and quantity readings, elision and retained numerical quantities are taught and practiced.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - Direct Object Pronoun + "y"
entries.evidence: Direct le/la/les before location y, l'y elision, and y before en are tied to actual complement roles; unrelated à-person substitutions are cautioned against.

entries.source_title: Using [preposition] + qui/lequel/laquelle/etc = on what/behind whom/beside which/etc (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Prepositions retain the actual verb/spatial relationship; things use agreeing lequel forms, while people accept qui or lequel. Items test person alternatives and sur/sans with things.

entries.source_title: Dont = Including/[quantity] of which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Shortened including clauses and full quantity-of-which clauses are taught; exercises check total-versus-subset interpretation and agreement with the relative clause's actual subject.

entries.source_title: Position of Double Pronouns in French - in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif)
entries.evidence: Post-verbal direct-before-person order, hyphens, moi/toi, m'/t' before en/y and restoration of ordinary order in negative commands all have teaching and constructed evidence.

entries.source_title: À + qui, auquel, à laquelle = to whom, what, which (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Complete auquel/à laquelle/auxquels/auxquelles series, actual à-selecting verbs and à qui alternatives for people; all four agreeing forms are exercised.

entries.source_title: De qui/dont/duquel = of/about whom, of/about which - with prepositional verbs with "de" (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Simple de-complement dont, de qui for people and formal inflected de-relatives are taught with usage preferences rather than bans. Exercises cover all three choices and eliminate redundant en.

entries.source_title: French reflexive pronouns can be used to express reciprocity - "each other"
entries.evidence: A dedicated lesson separates reflexive from reciprocal meaning, covers nous/vous/se and group on, explicit gendered/prepositioned each-other phrases and direct/indirect participle agreement.

entries.source_title: Duquel/de laquelle/desquels/desquelles with prepositional phrases with "de" (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Entire près de/à côté de/au bord de relations remain intact; all four de-lequel forms and person de qui alternatives are independently constructed.

entries.source_title: Depuis que + [conjugated verb] = (Ever) since + [conjugated verb] in French
entries.evidence: Finite-clause depuis que is distinguished from duration depuis; present continuing effects, completed starting events, past imperfect/pluperfect viewpoints and event counts prevent a one-tense rule.

entries.source_title: Malgré/En dépit de = Despite/In spite of in French
entries.evidence: Noun-phrase concession, no extra de after malgré, required de and contractions after en dépit are taught with register-sensitive discussion of clause alternatives.

entries.source_title: Soit ... soit ... = Either ... or...
entries.evidence: Fixed soit...soit pairs balanced infinitives, prepositional phrases or clauses. Exercises cover these structures; the rule avoids falsely imposing universal logical exclusivity.

entries.source_title: Pour que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = So that.../In order that... in French
entries.evidence: Purpose is distinguished from guaranteed result; shared-subject pour + infinitive contrasts with explicit-subject pour que + subjunctive, including completed future goals.

entries.source_title: Avant de + infinitive = Before + -ing in French
entries.evidence: Avant de requires an infinitive with a coherent shared subject; elision, different-subject avant que and optional non-negative ne are contrasted and checked.

entries.source_title: Dont = Whose (French Relative Pronouns)
entries.evidence: Possessive dont links people or things to a subject or object noun in the relative clause; the normal article replaces a redundant possessive, with both clause orders practiced.

entries.source_title: Bien que/quoique + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = although/though in French
entries.evidence: Bien que and one-word quoique select subjunctive while acknowledging real facts; present and past subjunctive exercises test both conjunctions and the factual-concession distinction.

entries.source_title: Merci de / pour = Thank you for in French
entries.evidence: Both noun prepositions remain accepted; infinitive de, elision, past-infinitive agreement and gratitude versus polite instruction are explicitly taught and independently exercised.

entries.source_title: Forming the superlative of French adjectives in complex cases
entries.evidence: Repeated articles with post-noun adjectives, pre-noun forms, ordinal ranks, de-introduced sets, full agreement and same-entity invariable le contrasts are taught; sentence construction tests the complete frame.

entries.source_title: Ainsi que = as well as, just as vs the way that in French
entries.evidence: Additive as-well-as and manner just-as readings are paired with translations; specified coordination versus parenthetical comparison determines fair plural/singular agreement tasks.

entries.source_title: Ce, cet, cette, ces + [durée] -là/-ci = that/those or this/these + [duration] (French Demonstrative Adjectives)
entries.evidence: Ce/cet/cette/ces selection, gendered time nouns, hyphenated -ci/-là and contextual reference are taught; this period, that summer and future ce jour-là readings are exercised.

entries.source_title: Faire + [infinitive] = to have something done in French (Causative)
entries.evidence: Dedicated lesson contrasts personally doing with arranging, teaches performer/affected-object roles and à/par alternatives, full present faire forms, pronoun placement, se faire and invariable causative fait.

entries.source_title: "Penser/trouver/savoir/croire/prétendre que" are followed with the indicative mood (L'Indicatif) in affirmative sentences BUT with the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) in negative ones
entries.evidence: All five named verbs are taught through assertion versus withholding. The index's categorical negative claim is explicitly qualified: negative savoir can preserve indicative facts, and stance matters in negative/interrogative opinions. Constrained keys preserve these legitimate readings.

entries.source_title: Attendre quelqu'un vs s'attendre à quelque chose = to wait vs to expect in French
entries.evidence: Full present patterns, direct-object waiting, reflexive à-expectation, same-subject infinitive and à ce que clause are taught; scheduled-arrival attendre is preserved as a legitimate expect reading.

entries.source_title: Avoir besoin que + the subjunctive mood (Le Subjonctif) = To need someone to do something in French
entries.evidence: A separately subjected besoin que clause selects subjunctive, while besoin de + infinitive/noun has a different complement. Exercises form the clause and retain de only where required.

entries.source_title: Expressing "the most/least that I have (ever)..." with a superlative followed by the subjunctive mood in French (Le Subjonctif)
entries.evidence: Subjective superlative relatives use present/past subjunctive according to meaning, with jamais as ever and object agreement. Indicative factual-set or asserted readings remain legitimate rather than categorically rejected.

entries.source_title: Expressing "the day after/the day before" in French with "demain/hier" vs "le lendemain/la veille" vs "le jour suivant/le jour précédent" (French Expressions of Time)
entries.evidence: Speaker-relative hier/demain contrast with narrative la veille/le lendemain and explicit jour précédent/suivant alternatives. Date-constrained items test all six expressions without automatic reported-speech replacement.

entries.source_title: Using negations with infinitive verbs in French indirect speech (French Negations)
entries.evidence: Reported demander de instructions, ne pas/plus/jamais/rien before infinitives, personne after its verb/preposition, pronoun-group placement and negative past-infinitive alternatives receive distinct constructed items.

entries.source_title: Comment ça se fait/Comment se fait-il que... ? = How come/How is it that...? (French Questions)
entries.evidence: Formal comment se fait-il que + conventional subjunctive, conversational comment ça se fait que with legitimate indicative/subjunctive readings, standalone questions and correct inversion punctuation are explicitly contrasted.
